hypothesis: A structural insight I hadn't used yet: both GAUC and nDCG@5 are purely *per-user* ranking metrics, so any feature that's constant across a user's own rows (e.g. user-level historical rate, user demographics) mathematically cannot change that user's ranking at all — it only shifts every one of their scores by the same constant. This is likely *why* iter 1's user-side features and the full CWM-13 user fields never helped: they can't move the metric by construction, regardless of how predictive they look in raw EDA correlations. What CAN move it is a feature that varies *within* a user's own row set — and the EDA already flagged one such signal that's never been added: session position (0→21+) within a user's day, which shows a real monotonic fatigue decline (0.41→0.31). I'm adding a leakage-safe, purely causal `pos_bucket` field to data.py: for each row, the 0-indexed count of impressions this user has already had *that day*, capped at 20, computed via chronological (hourmin, time_ms) ordering within each (user, date) group — this is known at serving time (just "this is the Nth video shown to this user today") and never crosses split boundaries since date ranges are disjoint per split.
reflection: The k-sweep (embedding dim) barely moved anything (+0.0001 GAUC, -0.0004 nDCG@5) and the bootstrap-noise probe (node 13, std≈0.0017, p5-p95 range≈0.0055) shows nearly every recent candidate has been within the metric's own sampling noise — further hyperparameter/regularization tweaks on the same 5-field bilinear FM are unlikely to produce a real, distinguishable gain.
expected_effect: I expect GAUC to move more than nDCG@5, because fatigue/position varies across essentially all of a user's rows (not just their top-5), giving the pairwise BPR loss a genuinely new within-user ranking signal across the full eligible-user comparison pool that GAUC aggregates, whereas nDCG@5 is dominated by the majority of valid users with <5 rows where session-position variance is minimal.
